outlook.method: Theil-Sen trend + Mann-Kendall test on 2001-2024 yearly data, extended to 2035 with an 80% prediction range. Where there is no clear trend, the 2001-2024 average is projected. Statistical extrapolation, not a climate-model forecast.

consequences.headline: Rain could fall 17% by 2035
consequences.detail: Yearly rain trends from about 2,092 mm to 1,742 mm.
consequences.action: Favour drought-tolerant crops and keep crop residue on the soil to hold moisture.

consequences.headline: Crops will need about 414 mm more water than rain gives
consequences.detail: Rain minus crop water demand moves from 743 mm to about 329 mm a year.
consequences.action: Plan irrigation or water harvesting, or shift to crops that need less water.

consequences.headline: In a dry year, rain can drop to about 1,423 mm
consequences.detail: That is 32% below the 2,092 mm average; about 1 year in 10 is this dry or worse.
consequences.action: Keep a drought-tolerant crop in the plan as insurance.

consequences.headline: +0.7 °C warmer on average by 2035
consequences.detail: The yearly average moves from 23.3 °C to about 24.0 °C. Most recommended crops stay inside their temperature range.
consequences.action: Watch heat stress in cool-climate crops; earlier sowing helps.
